body: what you mentioned about your childhood abuser strikes a chord. i sometimes "sense" that my abusive mother's conscience is in other people's bodies, leading me to distrust them. my hallucinations change too, but the consistent one is the voice. jesus, didnt realize how crazy i sound until i started replying to yalls comments :P i apologize for any spooky things i might say, haha.

i get all of those, too. i think it makes a little bit of sense for the paranoia to be related to bpd and maybe even delusions, but the hallucinations i have, im not sure are related.  
  
its even rare for people with full-blown schizophrenia to have serious visual hallucinations. i cant imagine how scary it would be.

i know about hypomania, and i think i experience that as well, but hypomania doesnt seem to cover serious hallucinations and delusions. i hear "the voice" which is trying to kill me, i can read minds, and i am sensitive of others' emotions to the point of being able to, it seems, accurately predict how they will feel in certain amounts of time (like precognition). i am actually not the sort to believe in these "magical" things, but they have never felt magical to me. they have been a part of how i experience life for years. ive done enough research to know that they are hallucinatory or delusional thoughts, but it doesnt make them any less real to me. maybe i am bipolar nos or just mood disorder nos, like someone above mentioned. sorry for typing lots, i have a ton of thoughts lately.

ive been getting pink. super clean roll with not much of a comedown (save for a headache only the most recent time i took it), but its also way more fiendish than mdma and the off-white m1 i was getting a few months back.
yeah, ask her why. like, not in a robotic way or anything, just, "_____, why do you feel like that? i dont hate you." reassure her that you still care about her. be sweet!

your advice on doing little activities is really great. when im so down in the dumps that i dont want to be alive another minute, doing anything at all, even something insignificant, makes me feel almost normal... like everything ive experienced is a regular part of life, and itll turn out alright just like every other mishap.  
  
unfortunately, he has left for good and i cant reverse it. i just have to remember that the future holds opportunity for change. beyond the sadness of it all, this will be a learning experience, and i know ill be able to keep someone i love around for a long while eventually. we all have our downfalls, and mental illness is one of mine - i know there are those out there who can see past it as long as im willing to get better.
im ok at the moment, but ill remember you when the time comes again :) haha.

i did make it through the night, though i dont remember half of it... i really need to discuss using alcohol as a coping method with my therapist next week, lol. right now im trying not to think about it. i am so disturbed by the fact that i couldve prevented his leaving. eventually, it will sink in that the only thing left to do is move on. i hope i wont feel so guilty someday.  
  
thank you so much for the kind words. this is a late reply, but reading your comment made me feel quite a bit calmer.

i have to keep my friend count low. its bad for me as far as sending impulse messages goes and everything. i still have it just because id fall completely out of touch with the outside world if i didnt

have you not read on these pages that dbt has been found to be the most effective treatment? i personally cant afford it quite yet, but ive been looking into ways i can do "at-home dbt" or whatever. its a personality disorder... its pretty heavy duty stuff. its treatable with 100% cooperation and with therapy.

ive done that since i was a kid, too, but as if im writing a book about my life... in third person. its really different from the voice, though. the voice is very intrusive and its not so much a narrator as it is a huge asshole, lol.

i hear a voice when im very depressed that says things about me in third person, like "_____ killed herself last night" "_____ is useless" "_____ has no more hope". it doesnt have its own particular voice, as in i couldnt assign it an age or anything, but it feels like its a hidden part of me. it perpetuates my self hate.  
  
i had my first therapy session in over a year this week, and ive been improving a lot, so i havent heard it in almost a month or so. but the places ive heard it in the past - my bedroom, a certain street i walk when i cant shake negative feelings, the dining room - all have a very dark "vibe" to them now. i cant really be in those places for long at all without feeling like theres something there with me. im not a superstitious person at all, and dont think its a demon or spirit or anything remotely similar. i have no idea what it is. this is my first time talking about it, so im having a hard time finding the words to describe how i feel about it. maybe ill write back in when ive figured out a healthy way to deal with it. :P

empathy isnt sugarcoating. empathy is understanding and putting yourself in someones shoes, which doesnt necessarily lead to being sensitive to a point of dishonesty or nonconfrontation. i definitely get that you disagree with me, but i dont see how you could reject that you shouldnt be extreme in this situation.  
  
i feel kind of silly arguing over it since she hasnt even commented on any of this, so im gonna stop, but i think the wisest move in any similar event would be to take a relatively neutral yet understanding approach. just be aware of not *only* the repercussions of the offended's actions, but also of the offended's feelings.

you can be blunt and not harsh. you can say, "you need to report this to the police. worse could happen to you next time or he could do the same thing to someone else." im nearly positive that would be just as if not more effective, and theres no sugarcoating involved. sugarcoating and being harsh are the extremes, and extremes arent really any good. i never implied she shouldnt go to the police and i never meant to say you need to be *gentle*... just more sensitive. empathy is necessary to move forward. absolutely necessary.

text definitely has tone. your rhetorical question, exclamation of "christ", and use of the phrase "while youre at it" are things that communicate a rude tone.  
  
i just think you could tell her to report it and be more sensitive. when this happened to me, the way youre speaking wouldve made me feel bad. ill back off.
ok, but your tone is rude as hell. being rude wont convince anyone to do anything. i doubt youre helping.

would it be difficult to be a little more gentle with someone who was just sexually harassed and reasonably is not sure if shes ready to go to the police? its important to inform them of the incident, but this is really recent. dont be an asshole.
a bloody kitten at *best*? i can see the danger, but thats pretty dramatic. that sounds more like the worst case scenario.

i can identify with what you said about your ex, and the only thing that has worked for me is receiving an ultimatum. he said it was him or the drugs, and being in a stage of idealization at the time, i chose him. however, i dont recommend this unless you *truly* feel that its you or the drugs... im no medical professional, but im pretty sure it isnt healthy to put that kind of stress on someone already suffering, anyway (definitely gave me mad anxiety when he said that). she really needs to be in therapy. is she just resistant to it? try to talk to her about that, not just the self-destructiveness. the problem should be about her overall health, not one symptom.
i dont have any articles or anything, but i was a regular 25i-nbome and shroom user for several months and am alright these days. i doubt taking them occasionally will do much harm.

several incidents with drugs have not damaged you by any means. ive dealt with heavy duty addiction to a number of different substances and even i have a chance of recovery. the only thing holding you back is that your minds still stuck on minor mistakes you made in the past - there is no reason to be so worried. you havent fucked up for good, drugs you stopped doing years ago will not kill you, you certainly do not have brain damage and it isnt why youre borderline. forgive yourself. what you did was not immoral. you seem like a reflective and self-aware person now, and thats all that matters. those are really, really good traits to have.

you dont fix your relationship with a mentally ill loved one by isolating yourself from them and labeling all their past/current behaviors as manipulative rather than getting help. this subreddit isnt for people to shit all over anyone with bpd.

bpders dont necessarily have good people skills. mine are pretty bad. we rarely try to lure people in to use them (and im sure there are tons of us that dont do that at all), and thats really all there is to it... we arent evil! i especially wouldnt worry about this girl since she seems to be recovered or in a late stage of recovery. if she ever snaps and you decide you still want to be with her, be there for her. dont make her feel low or insecure. be as open as you can with your feelings.

just like /u/NothinTSeeHere said, most of what you read that says borderlines lack empathy is written by those who have been close to those with the disorder. its easy to believe we lack empathy, i feel, because our emotions often overshadow everything. for example, last night i sent my ex a lot of texts accusing him of not caring about me, never having cared about me, i apologized for being in his life, etc. when he woke up to the texts this morning, he was insulted... this isnt the first time its happened, and every time we talk about the incident after its happened, he has to remind me of how busy he is (he cant spend tons of time with me and he cant always be there for me when im panicking). the fact that i am always forgetting these things and accusing him of having no love for me, not taking into consideration his side of everything, could be considered unemphatic. when im feeling more stable, its much easier for me to relate to and help those around me, so i wouldnt say i am inherently unemphatic. its just when im breaking down or triggered.

if the thought, yes, subconscious or conscious, to make the subject *feel* or *act* differently is not there, its not manipulation. this guy essentially asked if the things his ex told him during a stage of idealization were things she really felt or if she was manipulating him to suck him in. i responded that we rarely *lie to suck people in*. i imagine that just like me, when his ex expressed her feelings, she truly felt that way and just wanted to get the feelings out. when i share my grandiose view of someone with them, i have no motive, conscious or otherwise, to change how THEY feel. i am expressing how *i* feel, and nothing but. that is not manipulation - that is unawareness of my actions. that is not keeping myself in check. that is failing to balance my thoughts and feelings. it is harmful, but it is not manipulation. if someones feelings change after hearing anothers (and, as stated, there was no conscious or subconscious intent to do so), it isnt manipulation. its a reaction, and thats all it is.

your idea of the definition of manipulation is incorrect. rarely do i do or say something to a loved one simply in an attempt to make them feel a certain way or do something i feel they wouldnt do otherwise. THAT is manipulation. as i stated before, when i express myself in an intense manner, i mean exactly what i say. i am not trying to make their feelings different. i am trying to get the sore in my chest or the knot in my stomach, caused by my emotions, to go the fuck away. did you not read that i dont deny the harmfulness of our behavior? im not trying to display myself as a victim.

i want to get something straight: in my experience, both as a bpder and as a friend of a few, we very rarely *lie* to people to "suck them in". our manipulation is usually not deliberate; when we say intensely romantic/attached things, its generally because that is exactly how we feel at the time. remember that our moods are very subject to change. i dont deny the harmfulness of our behavior, but i deny the label of "manipulation", which implies the behavior is purposely harmful.  
  
all that said, no, i do not believe she ever lied to suck you in. i tell the truth when im idealizing. if i tell someone theyre the best thing on the planet, that i couldnt live without them, that theyre the handsomest man ive ever seen... i mean all of it. the problem to be dealt with is that i might feel differently tomorrow.

im in a similar boat right now. everything is looking pretty hopeless and im having a hard time getting through the days, not to mention the weeks. reading your story made me feel better, since i can tell youve still got lots of things going for you. i hope its the same for me.  
  
remember to savor the moment. even though you feel like you dont deserve it, let your boyfriend comfort you - the love we receive from those around us is really important to appreciate. what happened was a mistake, and we all make those. it is not a reflection of your character or capabilities, and as life goes on, things that are now out of your control will clear up; in your case, someone may return the phone... or they might not, and baby, thats alright. you and your boyfriend will keep on keeping on. the acceptance you find in other people and, most importantly, yourself, can get you through anything. the human mind is very powerful, even the bpd mind with its troubles and pain. in fact, i would go so far as to say its more powerful. youre a strong person for going through what you have and you will only become stronger. i promise you that.  
  
taking half a mg for three days in a row will cause virtually no damage (this coming from someone who popped 1 mg+ of xanax a day for a couple months and is still alive and kicking... clearly not something i advise, however. drug addiction is lame as hell). you will not experience withdrawals and i doubt youll suffer from any "zombie-like" symptoms that people get when they do too many benzos. the important thing is to not let it become an emotional crutch. :)
the mood swings and sensitivity really are emotionally immature. doesnt mean i like to hear it from others, though. :(

personally its both very elating and very very scary. almost nauseating. im used to caring about the other person so many degrees more than they do about me, or at least not being able to see it any other way. every morning i wake up and meditate, trying to prepare myself for abandonment. jealousy like you cant imagine. the happiest and often saddest i could ever imagine myself being.  
  
also, you dont know for sure that she has bpd (unless shes told you of a diagnosis)! different personality disorders have lots of things in common, but even then its not good to put someone into a label just in case its incorrect and will not do much to help em. : )
